hints.text: Rewrite $\tan^2\theta$ as $\frac{\sin^2\theta}{\cos^2\theta}$ and put everything over $\cos^2\theta$.

explanation: Take the identity $\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1$ and divide every term by $\cos^2\theta$.
So $1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta$ — the second member of the Pythagorean family.

alternativeExplanations.title: The third one comes the same way
steps: So there are three Pythagorean identities, and they are all the same statement divided by different things.
Tangent pairs with secant; cotangent pairs with cosecant — the "co" travels with the "co".
